hypothesis: One small post-extraction coordinator can make newly uploaded PDFs graph-ready by writing their supplied structural bundle, extracting reusable relationship signals, and persisting only references that pass the existing verification boundary.
implemented: verify immutable PDF hash and extraction-artifact identity before writing
write one supplied structural graph bundle through the existing idempotent writer
extract deterministic French and Arabic instrument-reference candidates
extract the existing provision and legal-action signals from the same pages
persist reviewed references only after existing rendered-page and target checks pass
reject stale review IDs, pre-populated reference edges, and unverified change events
return all unresolved signals as review-only candidates
conclusion: Keep the narrow coordinator. An existing upload worker can call it once per extracted PDF to add the document structure, obtain relationship signals, and persist reviewed citation relationships without adding a second extraction or ingestion framework.
limitations: This is a callable ingestion seam, not an HTTP upload endpoint, SQL job ledger, queue, or retry worker.
Legal-effect keywords remain NEEDS_REVIEW and do not automatically become REPLACE, MODIFY, ABROGATE, or other answer-bearing graph facts.
Complete temporal resolution still requires verified affected provisions, effective dates, and predecessor and successor versions in the supplied bundle.
The coordinator is implemented on the experiment branch and is not merged into main.
